business_problem: Misumi USA needed to handle about 2,000 inbound emails and more than 3,000 attached documents each day, but manual routing and document handling caused frequent misrouting, slowed order and quote processing, and made it hard to move away from legacy third-party services. Customers also struggled with an engineering-based configurator that supports 80 sextillion possible product combinations, while onboarding new web product categories took 3–6 weeks because critical knowledge was siloed.
solution_summary: Atos and Misumi designed a multi-part AI architecture around customer communications and e-commerce operations. Inbound emails and quote or order requests are classified with Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Amazon Bedrock so work can be routed automatically instead of triaged by hand. Bedrock Data Automation extracts key fields from more than 3,000 attached documents per day. A daily customer-data feed lands in Amazon S3 so the workflow can identify and code customers without constant API calls. Misumi's homegrown content management system was re-architected to use AI for duplicate-attribute detection and better data grouping, while Amazon Connect supports technical-support interactions and AWS Lambda / API gateway enables real-time CAD generation and UI updates in the React-based frontend. Together these components turn high-volume manual routing, extraction, and configuration work into agentic workflows.

solution_components.name: Bedrock Data Automation
solution_components.role: Extracts critical data from the thousands of attached documents that arrive with customer emails each day.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Stores the daily customer lookup feed used to identify and code customers without repeated API calls.

solution_components.name: Amazon Connect
solution_components.role: Supports technical-support call flows and provides a path for additional agentic voice AI integration.

solution_components.name: AWS Lambda / API gateway
solution_components.role: Enables real-time CAD generation and frontend UI updates in the React-based experience.

data_flow: Customer emails and attachments enter Amazon Bedrock workflows, where Claude 3.5 Sonnet classifies requests and Bedrock Data Automation extracts document data. The process enriches requests with daily customer records stored in Amazon S3, then routes work into Misumi's in-house order, quote, CMS, and frontend experiences, while Amazon Connect and AWS Lambda / API gateway handle support interactions and real-time UI actions.
business_outcome: Misumi automated high-volume email routing and document handling, achieved 80% classification accuracy in proof-of-concept testing, reduced the projected web category transformation timeline from 14 years to 2 years, and gained greater operational control by bringing specialized automation capabilities in house.
